answer: According to arXiv 2503.18983, the right to life under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) expressly protects individuals from "arbitrary" deprivations of life. The term 'arbitrary' deprivation is defined as involving an interference that is (1) not prescribed by law, (2) disproportionate to the ends sought, and (3) not necessary in the circumstances of the case considering the availability of less harmful means. This means that any deprivation of life must be justified and not occur without legal basis or in a manner that is excessive or unnecessary.
